name: Cynthia Bloom
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I still remember a memorial guest who only wanted to help chop vegetables.” On Saturday, near the blocks below Foundry Lofts, Cynthia checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I am arranging a meal instead of a ceremony. Everybody can come in the side door and leave separately.
appearance: Cynthia has short copper curls, a long face and high cheekbones, and a favorite piece of clothing, a washed violet jersey. It usually goes with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. When somebody else has the floor, Cynthia presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Cynthia finds names easy and faces hard on a crowded street. People who assume they have been snubbed usually get a warmer greeting once they speak.
agenda: To host a meal people can leave quietly.
family: Esther Mills is Cynthia’s cousin raised in the same household. Cynthia chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Esther brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The empty drum stool*, Esther says, “I recognized the handwriting as my old wife's.”
connections: Faye Tate. Fading flowers and a side-door meal give the family two ways to leave the memorial quietly.

reactions.situation: The victim's family wants a private anniversary meal
reactions.response: Cynthia lets the family make its own guest list and keeps press questions away from the table.

reactions.situation: A traveler asks for the last seat at the bus stop
reactions.response: Cynthia asks the person already using it whether they can comfortably stand, rather than presuming who needs it most.

reactions.situation: When somebody waves from across traffic
reactions.response: Cynthia waits at the corner to hear their voice and give them a proper answer.
